facts.F3: Hu Shen was dissolved by a Chinese agreement dated 12 January 1998, and the dissolution was registered with the Business Registration Office on 14 January 1998.

facts.F2: The applicant is required by the Securities and Future Regulations to maintain HK$18 million liquid capital which is 120% of the minimum liquid capital of HK$15 million.
facts.F3: The applicant ceased business on 20 April 2010 and sought the revocation of the licence and the release of the liquid capital requirement by the SFC.
facts.F4: The SFC would only be prepared to do so after the applicant has repaid all monies belonging to its clients and all unclaimed monies repaid or otherwise dealt with in accordance with an order of this court.
facts.F5: The applicant has produced various versions of client agreements that its clients had entered into with it, which provide that the applicant will act on behalf of the client to execute orders of leveraged foreign exchange trading given by the client.
facts.F6: The applicant has segregated its money from the clients' monies.
facts.F7: The applicant has by letter of 5 March 2010 notified all its clients at their last known addresses the termination of the client agreements, the applicant's cessation of business and that the clients should withdraw their cash balances from their accounts on or before 31 March 2010.
facts.F8: The applicant also ceased its business on 30 April 2010, and despite the notice, there were still some clients who had not taken their moneys back on 30 April 2010.
facts.F9: The applicant's staff then attempted to contact these clients by telephone asking them to get their moneys back, but some clients did not provide their bank account number to the applicant for transfer of their money, and some did not wish to have the return of their moneys.
facts.F10: On 14 January 2011, the applicant sent further notices to the clients with unclaimed moneys notifying them that the applicant would be making this application and asked them to get back their moneys on or before 28 February 2011.

facts.F9: The defendants were informed that the goods had arrived in Hong Kong on 5th June 1970, but they were not the engines that the defendants had ordered.
facts.F10: The bank debited the defendants' account with the amount of the drafts on 10th June 1970.
facts.F11: Various other transactions resulted in the account being overdrawn to the extent of $27,854.32.
